full_judgment: 4. Mr. S.H. Md. Nurul Huda Jaigirdar, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division without adverting to the evidence and findings of the Trial Court and the Court of Appeal below erroneously found that 'Jamiruddin executed the bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff in 1971 and he died in 1973. So it is immaterial to decide whether nor not Jamiruddin executed the deed in favour Rahim Balish in 1975' and the High Court Division further erroneously found that 'the defendants did not deny the execution of bainapatra by Jamiruddin and also failed to prove that Nasiruddin is not the son of Jamiruddin so the genuine-ness of the plaintiffs bainapatra and title deed remained unchallenged' although the High Court Division subsequently found that 'from the evidence of P.W.'s and D.W.'s it appears that the plaintiffs failed to prove that after purchase of the suit property in 1985 they went into possession of the suit property' and thereafter, the High Court Division erroneously found that 'since the plaintiff succeeded to prove their right and title in the suit property, though they failed to establish the fact of possession and dispossession, they are entitled to decree for khas possession.' The learned Advocate further submitted that the plaintiff failed to prayer by giving evidence that Nasiruddin is the son of Jamiruddin and that Jamiruddin executed a bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff but the High Court Division found that Nasiruddin is the son of Jamiruddin and that the plaintiff succeeded to prove the bainapatra executed by Jamiruddin. The learned Advocate also submitted that a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession, unregistered bainapatra does not create any title and the High Court Division found that the plaintiff accrued title in the suit property on the basis of the unregistered bainapatra.
